title: Eight-component N5 normal-order admissibility audit
question: Does the full eight-component harmonic number N^5 have a normal-ordered expansion whose every monomial lies within anisotropic Shubin order five, so that the R-167 graph estimate can in principle be applied without a hidden higher-order term?
method: Run the primary exact multicomponent Weyl normal-order implementation for d=1,2,3,8.
Run an independent multinomial reconstruction and independent ladder/tensor matrix lane.
Compare low-dimensional matrix powers with the normal-ordered expression on low blocks padded beyond the degree-10 boundary.
Compile Lean R280, which formalizes degree <= 10 implies anisotropic order <= 5, and enforce the QFT firewall in the integrated verifier.
finding: The primary, independent, and integrated lanes all pass. For d=8, N^5 has 1286 normal-ordered monomials, maximum total creation-plus-annihilation degree 10, anisotropic order 5. The coefficient absolute-sum diagnostic is 87496. The d=1,2,3 rows are respectively 5/20/55 terms with coefficient absolute sums 52/454/1866. Low-block matrix residuals are 0.0, 2.842170943040401e-14, 1.7053025658242404e-13, and 2.9103830456733704e-11 for the tested d={1,2}, low dimensions={2,3}; all are within the declared tolerance. Lean R280 compiles with two checked declarations. This closes only the combinatorial eight-component normal-order and order-admissibility subgate.
decision_reason: The normal-ordered monomial family has no hidden degree above ten, so the successor graph/domain step can be stated against an explicit finite family. The result is claim-nonbearing and does not instantiate a uniform graph constant or identify the actual Q3 form domain.
boundary: T0 claim-nonbearing combinatorial audit. It does not close the numerical uniform graph constant, q/p-to-creation-annihilation domain transfer, energy-to-number uniform form domination, eight-component Q3 Gibbs or evolved-history weighted-tail uniformity, source/volume/orientation/history uniformity, direct D-delta-D Cauchy control, common alpha, Hamiltonian-to-OS identification, KMS/GNS gap, continuum, C6, Sector A, or Pre-A.

adversarial_review.check: The d=8 lane is generated from eight independent oscillator components; no scalar fixture is silently promoted.
The primary contraction recurrence and the independent one-component/multinomial reconstruction agree on all tested component rows and the matrix lane.
Ambient matrix dimensions exceed the tested low blocks by the declared padding; the residuals remain below the agreement tolerance.
The finite order audit might be mistaken for the uniform R-167 graph estimate or q/p-to-a/a-dagger domain theorem.
A combinatorial normal-order identity might be cited as OS/KMS/GNS, mass-gap, continuum, C6, Sector A, or Pre-A closure.

next_action: Bind the explicit eight-component monomial family to the exact R-167 graph norm with a uniform constant on the canonical compact onsite-source set, then test the resulting energy-to-number form inequality on actual eight-component finite states before any Q3 state or QFT promotion.
